commit.message:
Phase 3.2: deterministic three-question Analyst orchestrator + weekly workflow

scripts/run_three_question_analyst.py now hosts the full pipeline:
TickerSession (12-call cap, dedup cache, trace builder), evaluate_q1/q2/q3
encoded as deterministic rules over Phase 2.5 collector outputs, a Critic
that emits PICK/WATCH/SKIP, and a markdown renderer for runs/{date}_react.md.
The Phase 3.1 helpers (compute_recovery_score, attach_recovery_score,
format_pick_header, sort_by_recovery_score) are unchanged.

.github/workflows/weekly-react.yml runs Friday 16:00 UTC — one day after the
Thursday weekly-screen cron — installs deps, runs the test suite, finds the
latest screen CSV, executes the orchestrator with --top 10 --no-commit, and
commits the resulting react.md back to the workflow branch.

CLAUDE.md gets a Phase 3.2 note clarifying that the weekly automated flow
is rule-based, not LLM-ReAct; LLM-ReAct stays available for local ad-hoc
deep-dives.

tests/test_three_question_analyst.py grows by 11 cases covering each Q1
verdict path, both Q2 horizons, both Q3 severity ends, both Critic outcomes,
and a synthetic-CSV end-to-end smoke that verifies markdown structure. All
tool calls mocked; no live network.

commit.message:
Phase 3 v3: three-question Analyst (mispricing → time horizon → risk)

Replace the five-criterion Analyst loop with a three-question framework:
Q1 mispricing real or market right; Q2 temporary or structural; Q3 single
biggest risk. Rule-based Critic verdict on top of Q1+Q2+Q3 outputs (PICK,
WATCH, SKIP). Hard cap of 12 tool calls per ticker.

commit.message:
Phase 2.5: evidence collector tools (SEC, Finnhub, FRED, peer reaction)

Replace tools/research.py with eight evidence-collector functions:
get_sec_filings, get_company_news, get_earnings_call_evidence,
get_analyst_revisions, get_insider_activity, get_peer_reaction,
get_governance_red_flags, get_macro_context. Each return value carries a
sources[] list with a source_tier field (A: SEC EDGAR / official PR,
B: Reuters/AP/Finnhub aggregated; tier C is dropped at ingest).

Tests rewritten to cover all eight functions with mocked HTTP responses;
no live calls.
